title: Which iPhone Photo Cleaner Fits Your Cleanup?
desc: Compare Apple Photos, Slidebox, Cleanup, Clever Cleaner, and Photo Cleaner: Swipe & Delete by task, review controls, and current purchase models.
heading: Choose a photo cleaner for the job you actually have.
intro: Start with Apple Photos for detected duplicates and simple manual deletion. Consider a dedicated cleaner when you want similar-shot review, swiping, or a focused cleanup plan.

sections.title: How this comparison was made
sections.html:
This guide is written by Mohamed Elatabany, the developer of Photo Cleaner: Swipe & Delete, so it has a commercial interest. It compares task fit using each app’s own listing and documentation, checked October 2026. It is not a performance benchmark, a ranking, or a guarantee about the amount of storage any app will recover.

Purchase options and feature availability change. Read the current listing and purchase screen before choosing. No competitor’s privacy or safety claim here substitutes for reading its full policy.

sections.title: Make the choice in three steps
sections.html:
1. Identify the task. Sorting albums, finding repeated shots, and freeing local storage are different jobs.
  2. Try the built-in Photos collections and inspect Settings → General → iPhone Storage. A cluttered grid does not always mean Photos is your biggest storage problem.
  3. If you need a dedicated review flow, try a small session before committing to a purchase. Check that you can understand what is marked for removal and review it before deletion.

For a personal plan and deliberate swipe decisions, Photo Cleaner: Swipe & Delete is worth evaluating. For organizing kept photos into albums, Slidebox may be a closer fit. For a detected-duplicates problem alone, Apple Photos may be enough.

Start with the cleanup planner to compare the estimated file bytes in the photos, screenshots, and videos you are considering removing.

sections.title: Safety applies whichever app you choose
sections.html:
Maintain a separate copy of irreplaceable media. iCloud Photos is a synced library: removing a photo also removes it from other synced devices. Recently Deleted usually provides a 30-day recovery window, unless you permanently remove the item earlier. Keep that window when possible.

Do not choose a cleaner based on claims that it will boost battery life, erase system caches, or guarantee a fixed number of gigabytes. The result depends on your library and what you actually choose to delete.

faqs.question: Do I need a paid app to delete duplicates?
faqs.answer: No. Apple Photos includes duplicate detection and merging. A dedicated app may help with similar shots or a different review workflow.

faqs.question: Which app will free the most space?
faqs.answer: That cannot be predicted without reviewing your library. File sizes, iCloud optimization, and the items you choose to remove determine the result.

title: Cleanup Alternative for a Personal Photo Cleanup Plan
desc: Compare Cleanup with Photo Cleaner: Swipe & Delete when you want a personal photo cleanup plan, deliberate swiping, and review before deletion.
heading: Looking for a Cleanup alternative? Start with your cleanup goal.
intro: Photo Cleaner: Swipe & Delete is an option if you want a personal cleanup plan and a deliberate swipe review. Apple Photos may already be enough if your only task is merging detected duplicates.

sections.title: What Swipe & Delete focuses on
sections.html:
The app helps you choose where to start: review duplicate and similar photos, old screenshots, and large videos, then follow focused sessions based on your priorities. Swipe right to keep a photo or left to mark it for removal. Undo a swipe or restore a marked item from the in-app Trash Bin before confirming deletion.

Photo analysis runs on your device; photos are not uploaded for scanning. Apple and RevenueCat handle purchase services. It is an iPhone photo-library app, not a system-cache cleaner or a promise to speed up your phone.

sections.title: Compare the tradeoffs fairly
sections.html:
Cleanup advertises a broader set of cleanup features in its own App Store listing. Read that listing if you want tools beyond photo review. Swipe & Delete’s focus is your photo library and personal review plan; this page makes no claim that it is faster, more accurate, or universally better.

Both apps offer in-app purchases. Swipe & Delete starts with a one-time free allowance; Pro unlocks unlimited swipes and advanced tools. Subscription and one-time purchase availability are shown inside the app. Check each app’s current terms rather than choosing from outdated comparison prices.

If video compression is essential, check whether a current product explicitly offers it. Swipe & Delete reviews large videos; this website does not claim that it compresses them.

sections.title: Try a small, safe session
sections.html:
1. Check Settings → General → iPhone Storage to see whether Photos is actually your biggest category.
  2. Open Apple Photos and check Duplicates. Merging detected duplicates may solve the problem without another app.
  3. If you want a plan or swipe review, try Swipe & Delete on a manageable category.
  4. Check the in-app Trash Bin before confirming deletion, and keep Recently Deleted as a recovery buffer.

For an estimate before opening any app, use the local-only cleanup planner. It shows which category contributes the most file bytes under the assumptions you enter.

With iCloud Photos enabled, deletion syncs across your devices. Keep a separate backup of irreplaceable files. Optimized originals may already live mostly in iCloud, so their full file size is not guaranteed local space.
